label: explain_concept
text:
KV caching is a speed trick used when an LLM generates text one token at a time.

In each layer, attention needs two vectors for every token already seen: a **key (K)** and a **value (V)**. Without a cache, the model would recompute K and V for the entire prompt and all previous output tokens on every new step. That work repeats and grows with the sequence length.

With KV caching, those K and V vectors are stored after the first pass. On the next token, the model only computes K and V for the new token and appends them to the cache. Attention then reads the full cached history plus that new pair.

The result is much faster generation, especially for long chats. The cost is extra GPU memory: the cache grows with sequence length, batch size, and number of layers. When memory runs out, systems may evict or recompute parts of the cache.
